routing.title: Routing strategy
routing.balanceHint: Rotate failover candidates by weight when enabled; off by default
routing.probeHint: Send one minimal real request to members in cooldown and lift the cooldown as soon as they answer; probes are billed, off by default
routing.weightsHint: Used when a group's mode is Weighted: each dimension is normalised then summed by weight; members with missing data take part with an optimistic prior. 0 disables a dimension - the weights do not need to sum to 100.
routing.speedHint: The complaint "speed is not great" has two halves: how long until the first token (TTFB) and how fast tokens come (throughput). The two thresholds decide who counts as slow, the strength decides how much traffic a slow member loses, and the first-event watchdog gives up on a slow member earlier instead of hanging until the group-configured 30s.
routing.speedWeightHint: A slow member is discounted geometrically by its excess (4x slower with strength 40 is about 57% weight). It only demotes, never excludes; 0 disables the speed dimension entirely.
routing.speedSlowTtfbHint: A member whose latest streaming first token exceeded this is discounted in proportion to the excess; 3000ms by default, 0 disables the TTFB criterion.
routing.speedSlowTpsHint: A member whose windowed output throughput is below this is discounted in proportion to the shortfall; 8 by default, 0 disables the throughput criterion.
routing.speedFeMultipleHint: The streaming first-token budget = min(group setting, that member's measured TTFB x this multiple), 4 by default. With too few samples the group setting is used, so a member's first use behaves exactly as before. 0 disables it.
routing.speedFeFloorHint: A small measured TTFB never pushes the budget below this (5000ms by default): it prevents one stray 40ms sample from cutting the budget to a few hundred milliseconds.
routing.allocateHint: Used when a group is set to Quota spread: each member gets traffic in proportion to its own remaining requests. Remaining requests come from the monthly quota (quota - used) first, otherwise from balance / per-request cost; members where neither is known join with the median weight of the known ones (unknown is never penalised).
routing.allocateTokensHint: When the request body yields an input-token estimate it is used directly; otherwise this value converts balance into "how many more requests".
routing.allocateHealthHint: Members with a low success rate, an attempt slower than the threshold, or a recent upstream throttle get their weight discounted by this strength; the floor stays 1, so it demotes rather than excludes (excluding is the cooldown's job). 0 means balance only, no health.
routing.allocateSlowMsHint: A member whose latest attempt exceeded this is discounted in proportion to the excess; 0 disables the latency discount.
routing.allocateMinRequestsHint: A member with fewer remaining requests than this is dropped from the candidates (less than one request left); 0 disables the quota cut.
routing.memberRpmLimitHint: We brake first: once a member reached this many requests in the last minute it steps aside for this round (if every member is at the limit they are still used). The upstream limit is unknown, so the default is unlimited.
routing.memberTpmLimitHint: Same as RPM but measured on tokens consumed in the last minute; a member at the limit steps aside for this round.
routing.throttleCapHint: On a 429 with Retry-After the cooldown takes the longer of the upstream hint and the group cooldown, capped by this value (300s by default) so a single bad response cannot freeze a member for long.
routing.monthlyAction: Action when the monthly quota runs out
routing.requestFaultAction: Action when the upstream rejects the request itself
routing.bodyLimitHint: How large a client request body the gateway will read. This used to be hard-coded to 64 MB: Codex remote-compact requests were rejected by our own gateway with an upstream-looking "request body too large" error, which is easy to misread as an upstream problem. Bytes; 0 means unlimited.
routing.bodyLimitHint2: Default 268435456 (256 MB); 0 = unlimited. The larger the limit, the more memory one big request costs (the body is held in memory and copied on every rewrite round).

modelMapping.title: Model Mapping
modelMapping.description: Clients often hard-code versioned model names (claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022) while local groups use short names (claude-sonnet), so the client gets model not found. Rules here rewrite the requested name into a target group name. When nothing matches, the original name is used unchanged — so behaviour is identical to before until you add a rule.
modelMapping.tryPlaceholder: Enter a model name a client would send, e.g. claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
modelMapping.noMatch: No rule matched — the group is looked up by the original name
modelMapping.empty: No rules yet. Without rules, clients must send a model name identical to the group name.
modelMapping.requiredHint: Rule name, match pattern and target group are all required
modelMapping.matchTypeHint: Exact = whole-name match (case-insensitive); wildcard supports * and ? (dots are literal); regex uses standard syntax. Higher priority matches first.

usageReport.title: Usage Reports
usageReport.description: Push a usage and cost summary to your configured notification channels (ServerChan / Feishu / DingTalk / WeCom / email / webhook) on a schedule. Each report covers the previous complete period (daily = yesterday, weekly = last calendar week, monthly = last calendar month) so the numbers never change after delivery; each period is sent at most once.
usageReport.hint: Send hour is a local-time hour (0-23). Reports only cover data already persisted to the database (see the stats save interval under Data & Backup), so the body states its data cutoff. Use Preview first to see exactly what you would receive.

alertRule.title: Alert Rules
alertRule.description: Metric-based alerts: notify your configured channels when a channel's error rate or average latency exceeds a threshold over a recent window. Complements the existing event notifications (balance hit zero, probe recovered) — failures are scattered, so there is no single event to hook onto.
alertRule.namePlaceholder: Rule name (e.g. "channel error rate too high")
alertRule.hint: Min samples is what keeps alerts quiet: below it nothing is evaluated, otherwise a single unlucky failure reads as a 100% error rate. Cooldown is per rule AND per channel, so one bad channel cannot consume another's alert budget.
alertRule.empty: No rules yet. Without rules no metric alerts are produced.
alertRule.channelRequired: A channel name is required when scope is "specific channel"
alertRule.noSamples: No samples in the window — nothing to evaluate yet

cliExport.description: Compose the relay URL, gateway key and group name into a snippet each client can paste directly. The gateway cannot reliably infer its own public address (reverse proxies and port mappings change it), so confirm the URL yourself before generating.
cliExport.modelPlaceholder: The model name clients send — i.e. the gateway group name
cliExport.hint: The output contains the key in plain text (that is what makes it useful) — do not paste it anywhere public.

trustedProxies.label: Trusted reverse proxies
trustedProxies.hint: Your reverse proxy addresses (e.g. 127.0.0.1 or 172.16.0.0/12), comma separated. When empty the gateway derives the source IP from the TCP peer only and ignores X-Forwarded-For entirely - that is the safe default, because honouring forwarded headers lets any client forge its source and silently defeats an API key's IP allowlist. Set this only when the gateway really sits behind a trusted proxy.

form.name: Group Name
form.modeHint: Manual fixes one member; failover follows member order and switches on failures; lowest cost tries the cheapest member first; quality first prefers the member with the best recent success rate; lowest latency prefers the member with the shortest recent attempt; least busy prefers the member with the fewest in-flight requests (same failover behaviour); lowest recent usage tries the member that consumed the least in the last minute (tokens first, then requests) to spread load and stay clear of upstream rate limits; quota spread shares traffic in proportion to each member's remaining requests (several small keys together carry the load of one big one).
form.smartThresholdHint: Only used by smart mode: the request complexity score (message rounds, input size, tool count) at or above this value goes to the earlier members (decision engine), below it to the later ones (execution engine). Default 50. Order members by preference - the strongest first.
form.tierHint: Smart routing tier: Auto = split in member order (existing behaviour); Decision = preferred for complex requests; Execution = preferred for simple ones. Click to cycle. Once any member declares a tier, the whole group follows declared tiers and undeclared members fall into the execution tier.
form.retryCountHint: Total attempts per member, including the first request
form.retryIntervalHint: Wait time between attempts on the same member
form.nonStreamTimeoutHint: Maximum wait for a complete non-stream response
form.streamIdleTimeoutHint: Longest allowed silence after the first stream event: if the upstream stops producing output, the response ends at this limit and the member is recorded as failed (the first byte is already committed, so there is no retry with another target). 0 disables the guard. Default 300 seconds; some relays are fake-streaming and only deliver the body once generation finishes, so raise it if a slow-but-alive stream gets cut.
form.streamTimeoutHint: Maximum wait for the first valid stream event
form.cooldownHint: Time a member is paused after retries are exhausted
form.affinityHint: Time to keep the fallback member after its first successful request
form.hedgeHint: Before committing the first byte, race the top-ranked members and use the first valid response; cooling or unavailable members stay out
form.hedgeCostWarn: Each hedged request may be processed by several upstreams - extra cost applies
form.hedgeWidthHint: Including the primary, 2-5; fewer than 2 lanes never races
form.hedgeAfterHint: Add hedge lanes when the primary produced no valid first response within this time; 0 disables the delay trigger
form.hedgePeakHint: Race immediately when the group's in-flight requests reach this value; 0 disables the peak trigger
form.nestedHint: Nested groups are flattened into their members at routing time; cooldown and affinity stay on the top-level group. A child group shows available when at least one of its members can forward
form.childHint: Child groups flatten into their members at routing time; self-reference and cycles are rejected by the backend
